title: Book One · Chapter 88: A Goal Made of Shoes
story:
The field is dry enough to play on again.

Dad comes with Ronan after lunch. They have no ball from a shop. Mum made a soft ball from old cloth. She tied the cloth inside a strong cover. It is not round on every side.

“It will choose its own way,” Dad says.

“So will you,” Mum says. She brought a cushion. She can mend it beside the field.

Leo arrives with his mother. She is on her way to work. “Can Leo walk home with you?” she asks Dad. Dad checks the time. Then he agrees.

The boys put two shoes on the ground for a goal. They keep their own shoes on. These are Dad's old shoes. He brought this spare pair in a bag.

“That goal smells,” Leo says.

“Then do not put your nose in it,” Dad answers.

Ronan laughs so hard his first kick misses the ball completely.

They play two against one. Dad must walk. He cannot run in this game. He runs too fast for the boys. Leo makes this rule. “Do not move a shoe,” Ronan adds. “The goal must stay this size.”

“Such a hard life,” Dad says.

At first the boys rush together at every kick. The ball goes between them. Dad walks slowly up the field and scores.

“You were both there,” he says.

“You were not there,” Leo tells Ronan.

“You pushed me.”

Mum looks up from the cushion. “I am not the judge.”

The boys stand apart. Dad gives them the ball again. This time Leo waits on the left. Ronan kicks towards him. The cloth ball turns away from Leo. It stops short of Leo.

Leo runs back and kicks. It passes just outside the shoe.

“Nearly,” Ronan calls.

They try again. It takes many tries. At last the boys score. Dad falls onto the grass. He pretends their kick made him fall.

“That was a very strong kick,” he says.

“It only touched you a little,” Leo says.

“Then I am not very strong today.”

Dad is smiling up at them. Ronan can see the smile. Dad is not really hurt. He pulls one arm while Leo pulls the other. Dad makes a lot of noise as he gets up.

After a rest, Ronan asks for a game with only the two boys. Dad sits beside Mum. He watches quietly. He gives no advice about their kicks.

Leo is faster. Ronan waits near the goal. He does not run after each kick now. The score stays close. A little child walks near the goal shoes. They stop playing. They wait for his mother to walk away with him.

The sun moves behind the trees. Mum finished one side of the cushion. Dad checks the time. “We need to take Leo home,” he calls.

Ronan wants one last kick. Leo wants three. They agree on one each.

Neither kick scores. They pick up the shoes and the uneven ball. Ronan carries Dad's bag even though the goal still smells.

On the walk back, Dad and Mum talk about supper. Leo walks backwards to show them a new step. Dad asks him to turn round. Ronan ran a lot. His legs are sore, but he feels happy. No one made anything to sell today. He wants to play here with them again.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- goal＝球门
- score＝进球、得分
- judge＝裁判
- two against one＝两人对一人

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：cushion＝坐垫；spare pair＝备用的一双；sore＝酸疼的。

## 读句提示

**Can Leo walk home with you?**

Leo能／和你们一起／走回家吗？直接询问，不嵌在asks whether里。

## 理解问题

1. 孩子们怎样让与Dad的比赛较公平？
2. 本章里哪些快乐与挣钱、做项目无关？
